name: Nadëb
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: O Nadêb é uma língua de acento fixo, o qual incide sempre na última sílaba da palavra, conforme se pode verificar nos exemplos em (100). (100) /ta 'wog/ 'barriga dele' /ba 'ho:d/ 'vento' [p. 49] ... Constatou-se que o Nadêb é uma língua de acento fixo, o qual recai sempre na última sílaba da palavra, e que o acento é responsável pelo processo fonológico caracterizado por redução da duração vocálica, se esta for uma vogal longa e se encontrar em sílaba pré-tônica. [p. 57]
new_statements.translation: Nadêb is a fixed-stress language, with stress always falling on the last syllable of the word, as can be seen in the examples in (100): /ta'wog/ 'his belly', /ba'ho:d/ 'wind'. ... It was established that Nadêb is a fixed-stress language, with stress always falling on the last syllable of the word, and that stress is responsible for the phonological process of vowel-length reduction when a long vowel stands in a pretonic syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word; non-contrastive. Long vowels do not surface (are shortened) in open pretonic syllables, and only reduced vowel allophones [ɪ ə ʊ] occur there. The language has no tone; vowel length and laryngealization are the contrastive suprasegmentals. Independently confirmed for the Roçado and Rio Negro dialects by Martins 2005 (LOT 104), sec. 2.2.4 p. 69: 'Os dialetos Nadëb têm um sistema acentual fixo na última sílaba' and 2.2.5 'Os dialetos Nadëb não possuem tons'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in Barbosa 2005 or Martins 2005.
new_statements.exceptions: Proclitic (non-independent) personal pronouns are phonologically bound and unstressed (Barbosa p. 54; Weir 1984). Weir 1984 notes most verbal suffixes are monosyllabic and unstressed while the suffix manɨh is stressed on its second syllable, and incorporated elements keep their own stress -- i.e. the stress domain is the phonological word/root plus stress-bearing suffixes; no lexical exceptions to final stress are reported.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('última sílaba da palavra'), illustrated with citation forms including possessor-proclitic + noun (/ta'wog/ 'his belly') where the proclitic is unstressed and stress is final. Barbosa's data are from the Paraná Boá-Boá (Jutaí community) variety; Martins 2005 gives the same rule for the Roçado and Rio Negro dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: Barbosa 2005 describes the Nadëb variety of the Paraná Boá-Boá Indigenous Territory (Jutaí community, Japurá basin); Martins 2005 covers the Roçado (upper Uneiuxi) and Rio Negro (Bom Jardim, 'Kuyawí') dialects and states the same fixed-final rule for both, so the statement holds for Nadëb (nade1244) as a whole. Glottolog lists no separate dialect codes that need distinguishing here.

sources.note: Ch. 4 'Propriedades supra-segmentais', 4.1 Acento (p. 49): Nadêb is a fixed-stress language, stress always on the last syllable of the word (exx. /ta'wog/ 'his belly', /ba'ho:d/ 'wind'); repeated in Considerações finais p. 57, adding that long vowels shorten in open pretonic syllables; proclitic pronouns are unstressed (p. 54). No tone. Data: Paraná Boá-Boá (Jutaí) variety, author's own fieldwork.

(141); 2.2.5 p. 69-70: 'Os dialetos Nadëb não possuem tons' -- length and laryngealization took over the function of Proto-Eastern-Makú tone.

sources.note: 'Fonologia e ortografia' (pp. 13-14) gives only the segment inventory plus length and laryngealization features; no statement of word-stress placement. Scattered morphosyntactic remarks: proclitic pronouns never stressed; most verbal suffixes monosyllabic and unstressed, manɨh 'sempre é acentuado na segunda sílaba'; incorporated elements keep their own stress, prefixes unstressed.
